title: Patient Financial Services Manual — Statement Series, Final Notice and Agency Placement
content:
**3.1 Clauses no longer in force.** The following clauses of this Patient Financial Account policy are no longer in force and have been superseded by the current basis:

- (a) the clause that issued a statement every statement cycle of the tier while a balance is owed, numbered within the current unpaid series, with any payment or copay collection restarting the series;
- (b) the clause that left charges whose claim is still pending with the payer off statements until the insurance-pending hold after their date of service had run, and that never statemented or escalated charges enrolled in an active payment plan while the plan was active or delinquent;
- (c) the clause under which enrolling the past-due balance in a payment plan, or paying it below the placement minimum, during the final-notice period returned the account to active.

The per-class figures these clauses named (statement cycle, insurance-pending hold, placement minimum) remain the figures of the financial classes.

**3.2 Statuses that receive statements.** Statements are issued only while the account status is active or precollection, as the account record shows at the time of issue. An account on billing hold is never statemented, noticed or placed.

**3.3 Final notice.** The unpaid-statement count is the number of statements issued on the account and dated from the later of the account's activation and its most recent payment or time-of-service collection, up to the handling date. When that count reaches the tier's number of unpaid statements before final notice, the final notice is issued and the account moves to precollection. If at that moment the remaining past-due balance is at or below the tier's small-balance write-off level, it is written off with an adjustment coded as a small-balance write-off instead, and no final notice is issued.

| At the moment the count reaches the tier's number | Result |
|---|---|
| remaining past-due balance above the write-off level | final notice issued; account to precollection |
| remaining past-due balance at or below the write-off level | balance written off as a small-balance write-off; no final notice |

**3.4 Final-notice period.** The final notice was issued at least the tier's final-notice period before the placement date. The final-notice period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the final notice date, and placement is allowed on the day the period ends, not before. The final notice date is the one recorded on the account.

**3.5 Placement minimum.** Placement additionally requires a past-due balance at or above the tier's placement minimum; a smaller balance stays in precollection and keeps receiving statements.

### Worked boundary (hypothetical dates, a 30-day final-notice period)

Final notice dated day 0. Day 1 is the first counted day and day 30 the last.

| Proposed placement date | Period elapsed? |
|---|---|
| day 29 | no — placement not allowed |
| day 30 (the day the period ends) | yes |
| day 31 | yes |

Placement on day 30 still needs the past-due balance at or above the placement minimum and an account not on billing hold.

superseded_clauses: While a balance is owed, a statement is issued every statement_cycle_days of the account's tier, numbered by statement_sequence within the current unpaid series; any payment or copay collection restarts the series.

Charges whose claim is still pending with the payer are left off statements until insurance_pending_hold_days after their date of service, and charges enrolled in an active payment plan are never statemented or escalated while the plan is active or delinquent.
Enrolling the past-due balance in a payment plan, or paying it below collections_min_balance_usd, during the final-notice period returns the account to active.
